findings.note: Omitted by V14, reopened by the revision. A reverse guard (also run by task lint:observability) resolves every series a Prometheus panel or a loaded rule reads to a metric the code defines, a recording rule or a declared external producer whose scrape job is configured; it was red on exactly the four orphan panels before the change. The two product panels read two gauges the hourly rollup computes in PostgreSQL over the North Star's useful set (tested on real PostgreSQL) - an observation histogram was rejected, since an outcome rejected after its validation cannot be taken back out of one; the two hybrid memory search panels were removed, their producer gone since v1.25.30 (ADR-168). Decision on alerts-product.yml: the freshness alert joined the core as ProductAggregatesStale (warning, runbook, promtool cases, evidence recipe); the three behaviour alerts stay unloaded and are re-decided by 2026-12-15 on a read-only measurement of production (ADR-178 amendment 2026-10-23). The coverage ratchet reads only the rule files prometheus.yml loads; measured, no metric was wired by a dormant rule alone (baseline unchanged).

appearances.title: AC-023 — Borner la répétition d'une compilation sémantiquement refusée
AC-023 — Borner la répétition payante d'une compilation de règles sémantiquement refusée

findings.note: A refused compilation of the read rules (a denial quoting words the person never wrote) is cached under the inputs' signature as a refusal that reads nothing; the run settles skipped with the reason rules_refused (a NOTHING_INTERPRETED outcome, a sentence in six languages) instead of failed. The same inputs are compiled again only after DISCUSSION_RULE_REFUSAL_FIRST_WAIT_INTERVALS tick intervals, then twice as long at each refusal, up to the cache lifetime (owner decision Q4); other inputs, or inputs that compiled last, start from one refusal. Measured before the change: the refusal raised before the cache was written, so every tick paid the compiler again for the same inputs.

appearances.title: AC-028 — Borner côté PostgreSQL l'attente de verrou et les transactions inactives

findings.note: Every application connection starts with lock_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (DATABASE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_IDLE_IN_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS; 0 = the server's own; the migration engine and the LangGraph pools carry neither; SET LOCAL still tightens one per transaction). The engine counts each bound reached in handle_error (db_bound_reached_total, alert DatabaseBoundReached): by SQLSTATE, except the idle end that asyncpg reports with none (measured), recognised by the idle span the engine kept. Calibration was limited: production keeps no transaction-length or lock-wait series of the exporter, so the bounds are conservative and the tail is now measured (buckets to 600 s).

appearances.title: AC-029 — Rendre propriétaire le verrou de rafraîchissement OAuth et l'aligner sur sa section critique
AC-029 — Durée totale du refresh OAuth non bornée par le calcul du bail

findings.note: The lock is not made an owner: it is gone. One refresh door for legacy connectors, shared grants and Hue Remote: one exchange per token (single flight in a worker, an owner-token claim across workers, a published verdict), no transaction across the provider call, a write conditioned on the token it started from and bounded in its wait for the row, invalid_grant re-verified before a disconnection. Residual, written in the ADR-302 amendment: callers reading through get_connector_credentials on a session they hold keep their read transaction during a rare refresh. Reopened by V15: the lease is derived from a per-phase HTTP timeout, and a response delivered in small fragments outlived it (17 s against a 13 s lease, local probe, no real OAuth server). The 2026-10-23 remediation (one refresh door, conditional writes, short sessions) stands; the total duration is not bounded yet.

appearances.title: AC-030 — Arrêter l'érosion de la couverture backend (marge 0,66 point)

findings.note: The lines a change adds or modifies are held at the floor (AC-030a, diff_coverage.py, in CI). The margin (AC-030b): measured on 2026-10-23, the unit suite alone covered 78.97 % of src and the SQL-bound domains sat far below the floor in it (sms 53.6 %, proactive discussions 70.7 %), while their integration tests on a real PostgreSQL covered them at 92.1 % and 82.4 %: meeting the floor in unit tests would have meant simulating PostgreSQL, which the test rules forbid. Owner decision 2026-10-23: the floor, unchanged, applies to what the unit and integration suites execute together, and the diff gate reads that union. Each suite measures into its own data file, combined strictly (a missing one is an error) outside coverage's implicit pattern; measured by the canonical commands, the union covers 87.47 % of src. Tests were added only where neither suite covered (the feedback route through HTTP, the reply receipts).

appearances.title: AC-033 — Fiabiliser le banc de tests : délais, oracle temporel et tests jamais exécutés

findings.note: A hung test is interrupted with its stack, every workflow job is time-bounded, the two never-run tests run (L2). The CPU linearity oracle (A12): three guards carried their own copy of the same criterion and one timed a single call per size on time.thread_time, which Windows advances by 15.6 ms ticks; they now share tests/support/cpu_growth.py (the thread's cycle-precise clock, interleaved pairs, the median pair, the floors), pinned on a scripted clock and refused a real quadratic function — sized so its small run clears the small floor, under which the criterion was measured to pass a quadratic function (1.5 ms to 26.5 ms read x5.3). A wall-clock oracle found flaky under the full suite (a held claim's refresh count after a fixed sleep) waits for the refresher instead.

appearances.title: AC-035 — Sortir les E/S disque bloquantes des fonctions asynchrones et outiller la règle

findings.note: Ruff ASYNC2 is selected for src with no baseline and no noqa (tests are exempt by path: the rule guards the served loop). The three STT file uploads stream a multipart body framed byte for byte as httpx frames it, every read in a worker thread through LocalFileRead: measured before the fix, every read ran on the loop and a witness task never ran during one; after it, the file is closed on an answer, a refusal and a cancellation, after the read in flight. The 12 path sites moved their whole step off the loop (the export fence renames inside its cleanup so a cancelled rename publishes nothing; the three copies of the stored-document path check became owned_document_path). Residual, measured by an AST census: Ruff types no path a helper returned, and 82 plausible synchronous filesystem calls sit in async bodies out of its reach. Nearly all are the brief metadata calls the finding ruled out (stat, resolve, a stored file's open, an unlink); two move content — the browser screenshot write in agents/api/service.py and a skill directory's rmtree in skills/router.py — proposed as a follow-up.

appearances.title: AC-036 — Aligner les gabarits d'environnement sur les défauts du code ou justifier chaque écart

findings.note: Owner rule: the database overrides the environment, which overrides the code's constants. Every template line states the code's default, omits the key, or says why it differs; a guard holds it, refuses a stated (default: X) the code contradicts (29 per complete template did) and loads each template, its secrets filled in, through the settings' validators. Owner decision 2026-10-23: the two complete templates carry production's proven tunable values (never a secret, an identifier, an address, a host or an environment's identity); the eight features of the initial decision are on, the analytics and the opt-ins documented on 2026-08-06 (MFA, peers, paid telephony, the arousal-relaxation safeguard) stay at the code's default, each annotated; the BACKGROUND_RUNS_ENABLED line left the minimal template. The proven-in-production annotations list where the code's defaults lag behind production: moving those defaults is the owner's call, outside this wave.
